Theme

Latin word

praecipuus

praecipuus, praecipua, praecipuum

adjective

main, chief, principal; chief, main, principal; special, particular, beyond the ordinary

In this lexicon

  • main

    the recommended word · classical · Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum; Quint. 1.3.1: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est

  • major

    also used · classical · Quint. 1.3.1: ingeniī signum in parvīs praecipuum memoria est; Tac. Dial. 28.4: cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum

  • special

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.12: praecipuum quendam amōrem; Caes. BG 5.54.4: praecipuō semper honōre

Examples

  • cujus praecipua laus erat tuērī domum et īnservīre līberīs

    whose chief praise was to look after the house and devote herself to the childrenTac. Dial. 28.4

    In the entry for main

  • et, id quod caput est, nōbīs inter nōs nostra sīve incommoda sīve vitia sīve injūriās esse tolerandās

    and, what is the main thing, that we must bear with one another’s annoyances, faults and wrongsCic. Att. 1.17.4

    In the entry for main

  • ingeneratque in prīmīs praecipuum quendam amōrem in eōs quī prōcreātī sunt

    and above all nature implants a special love for those one has brought into the worldCic. Off. 1.12

    In the entry for special

  • praeter Aeduōs et Rēmōs, quōs praecipuō semper honōre Caesar habuit

    except the Aedui and the Remi, whom Caesar always held in special honourCaes. BG 5.54.4

    In the entry for special
